story.logline: A voice defines luxury eight times, each definition finishing somewhere it should not, until one is so private it can only belong to one person — then the room empties and the definition is handed to you.
story.text:
Luxury is not a checklist. So we never show the checklist.

A voice — unhurried, amused — starts 'luxury is,' and every time the sentence finishes somewhere it should not. A man reads the paper in a bathtub on a roof, snow falling, steam holding its shape. A woman eats breakfast alone at a table set for twelve. A cellist plays to a drained pool, water still at her ankles. Nobody explains. The sets do it.

One thing crosses every room: a warm yellow. A robe, a lampshade, a single lemon on marble. Always the same yellow, never the same object. That is the only continuity we give you.

The definitions get more private as they go, until one is so specific it belongs to exactly one person — a man in a lit walk-in closet, choosing nothing, just standing there. Hold on it. Let the cut stop opening out and land.

Then hand it over. Last frame: the same room, the figure gone, the yellow still there.

beats.name: The voice starts
beats.what_happens: Black, then one centered tableau. The voice says 'luxury is' and does not finish. Symmetrical, small figure, room reads first.

beats.name: Ordinary rooms, made impossible
beats.what_happens: Bathtub on a snowing roof. Paper, steam, no shiver. The first definition lands and the set is abandoned on the cut.

beats.name: The yellow arrives
beats.what_happens: A single lemon on black marble, then a robe two rooms later. Same hue, different object. The viewer notices before anyone says it.

beats.name: Alone, on purpose
beats.what_happens: Breakfast for one at a table set for twelve. Deep focus, eye-level, centered. The emptiness is the luxury; nobody says so.

beats.name: The absurd escalation
beats.what_happens: A cellist plays to a drained pool, ankle-deep in what is left. Low wide angle. The definitions have stopped being reasonable.

beats.name: The closet — choosing nothing
beats.what_happens: A man in a lit walk-in closet, hands at his sides, choosing nothing. Slow push-in. The cut stops opening out and holds past comfort.

beats.name: Handed back
beats.what_happens: The same closet, figure gone, one yellow sleeve still on the rail. 'For you to define.' Hold, then out.

shot_seeds: Wide symmetrical tableau, clawfoot bathtub centered on a flat snow-covered rooftop, a small figure reading a newspaper, steam holding its shape in still air; slow push-in, eye-level, deep focus; soft overcast key at 2:1, cool #2E4E7E cast on the snow, one warm #E7B93A towel folded on the rim.

Centered wide of a twelve-seat dining table, one woman eating breakfast at the near end, eleven places set and untouched; locked slow dolly in, eye-level, deep focus; large window light from camera-left, low contrast, warm #E7B93A lampshades running the length of the table.

Low wide angle, drained infinity pool, a cellist playing mid-basin with a shallow film of water at her ankles, hilltop villa behind; slow push-in, deep focus, figure small enough to read the whole basin; hard late-afternoon key, #3E6F5E planting on the deck, #E7B93A cushion left on a lounger.

Slow push-in on a man standing centered in a lit walk-in closet, hands at his sides, choosing nothing, rows of garments symmetrical either side; eye-level, shallow focus falling off past his shoulders; warm practical strip lighting, 3:1, one #E7B93A sleeve breaking the neutral rail.

Static wide, the same walk-in closet, empty, everything identical except the figure is gone; no movement, deep focus; unchanged warm practicals, soft bloom on the rail chrome, the single #E7B93A sleeve still hanging center frame.

craft.register: This is a glossy luxury-commercial. Everything in frame is chosen, maintained and expensive: the architecture, the materials, the furnishings, the finish of every surface, and the condition they are all kept in. Nothing is improvised, makeshift, cheap, worn-out, novelty or comic. If an object would not appear in this world, it is not in the picture.
craft.look_clause: glossy luxury-commercial · digital, clean (no stock emulation) · medium-high contrast · low fine grain · subtle bloom around windows, skylights and practicals halation · palette #EDE6D6 warm cream, #B4506A dusty rose, #4FB0B0 pop teal, #E0A81E luxury gold · motivated natural light — big windows, skylights and backlight carry most spaces · soft, wrapping · key:fill varies by vignette: high-key/near-even in the pool, hoverboard and closet; low-key chiaroscuro in the ballroom and elevator · motivated by windows, chandeliers, floor lamps and wall sconces as practicals · HUE LOCK: warm daylight as the default, with a cool blue reserved for the moody vignettes (moon, ballroom)
craft.camera_clause: wide establishing (~24-35mm feel), detail inserts (~50-85mm feel), one low ultra-wide for the pop room only · clean digital-cinema look styled as a high-end real-estate / commercial reel; AI-generated, so no true lens — the feel is anamorphic-flavoured widescreen · crisp and glossy; high-key in the daylight spaces, moody chiaroscuro in the ballroom and elevator; minimal grain · mostly deep for the interiors so the whole space reads; shallow on the detail inserts (shoes, hands, bow tie, teacup) · eye-level to slightly low; strong central symmetry favoured; one dramatic low ultra-wide for the pop-room dance · moves: slow push-in, slow orbit/arc, locked wide with the subject moving inside it, tracking follow (hoverboard) · centre the hero space symmetrically · let the architecture frame the subject (arches, columns, doorways, the lift box) · leave negative space early for the on-screen serif word

script.line: No suit, no shuttle, just custom flooring.
It's overboarding because walking is so par.
Perhaps it's dancing in a ballroom meant for two.
Or it's the kind of style that makes walls blush.
A conversation between privacy and silence.
It's a pool with no screaming children.
Maybe it's living like a queen or a room that matches your groove.
It's an outfit for every mood.
For Mr. Shinoy, it's Heidi in an elevator.
elements luxury living for you to define.

morphs.rule: Every vignette ends by admitting it is absurd: on the LAST shot of each definition the person's head is an animal's, on their own human body, in their own clothes, in the same room, held in the same composure. Nothing else in the frame acknowledges it.
morphs.how: Anatomical, not costume. Real fur, real hide, real eyes, correct bone structure, scaled to a human neck and sitting naturally on the shoulders. Photographed absolutely straight — the same lens, light and grade as every other shot. No mask, no helmet, no headpiece, no seam at the neck, no fancy dress, no comedy, no CGI sheen. The film does not wink.
morphs.why: Danney, 2026-07-28: the concept that makes this ours rather than the reference's.
morphs.technique:
THE CHANGE HAPPENS BEHIND SOMETHING. Danney, 2026-07-28: *"when Naruto does his clone technique there's a poof cloud out of nowhere to cover the part that is morphing — when the smoke goes away it's revealed the new identity."* That is the right mechanism and the reason is technical: a generator is poor at morphing a face and good at occluding one. Interpolating a human head into an animal's over a second and a half gives you mush; hiding the instant of change behind something gives you two easy halves and one clean reveal.

What it must NOT be is a puff of cartoon smoke. This film's register forbids anything novelty or comic, and its own edit forbids dissolve, wipe and whip pan — so the cover is never an effect. It is a REAL OBJECT ALREADY IN THE ROOM, moving through the frame in front of the head: steam, a garment, a bow arm, spray. Same structure as the poof, dressed as the film.

locations.name: snowing rooftop
locations.note: The open-air roof deck of a tall building, outdoors under open sky, with a clawfoot bathtub standing in the middle of it. Nothing overhead — no ceiling, no canopy, no pergola, no glass roof: falling snow lands on every surface because the sky is directly above. Flat roof, snow lying deep and undisturbed underfoot, a low parapet at the edge and the city dropping away beyond it to a far horizon. Steam holds its shape in the still cold air. A cool #2E4E7E cast on the snow.

fields.scale: a roof deck wide enough to walk around the tub freely — the tub reads small against it; open sky above and the whole city below the parapet
fields.materials: snow over stone paving, a low glass-and-steel parapet, warm timber and lit glass at the penthouse wall behind
fields.mood: still, hushed, absurdly comfortable in the cold
fields.continuity: always OUTDOORS and always open to the sky; never an interior, an atrium or a covered terrace

locations.name: twelve-seat dining room
locations.note: A long table set for twelve with eleven places untouched, large low-contrast window light from camera-left, warm #E7B93A lampshades running its length.

locations.name: drained infinity pool
locations.note: An emptied infinity pool at a hilltop villa with only a shallow film of water left in the basin, #3E6F5E planting on the deck, hard late-afternoon light.

locations.name: lit walk-in closet
locations.note: A closet with symmetrical rows of garments either side and a neutral rail under warm practical strip lighting, identical whether the figure is present or gone.

characters.name: man in the bathtub
characters.note: A man in his fifties about to get into an outdoor bath, and completely at ease about it — bare shoulders and bare feet, a heavy waffle-cotton robe worn open and loose over nothing, sleeves pushed up, belt hanging untied. Damp hair. No coat, no knitwear, no trousers, no shoes, no socks, no watch — nothing he would have taken off to bathe. Calm, faintly amused, unbothered by cold.

fields.wardrobe: open waffle-cotton robe over bare skin, untied belt, barefoot — bathing, not dressed
fields.continuity: the same man and the same robe in every rooftop shot; he never gains a layer, because he is in a bath

characters.name: woman at breakfast
characters.note: A woman eating breakfast alone at the near end of a table set for twelve; the script gives no physical description.

characters.name: the cellist
characters.note: A woman playing cello mid-basin in the drained pool, ankle-deep in the water that is left; no further description is given.

characters.name: man in the closet
characters.note: A man standing centered in the lit closet, hands at his sides, choosing nothing — the one definition private enough to belong to a single person; his face is never described.

props.name: the warm yellow
props.note: A recurring warm yellow (#E7B93A) that appears as a different object each room — a towel, a lemon on black marble, a robe, lampshades, a cushion, a sleeve — always the same hue, never the same object; the film's only stated continuity.

props.name: clawfoot bathtub
props.note: A freestanding cast-iron clawfoot tub, full size — long enough for a grown adult to lie back in with room to spare, its rim at about mid-thigh on a standing person. Standing impossibly on the open snowing rooftop, filled with steaming water.

fields.materials: cast iron, glossy white enamel inside and out, polished chrome feet and taps
fields.scale: 170–180cm long, rim ~60cm off the ground — an adult fits lying down, shoulders under the rim. NEVER a small, toy or tub-shaped basin.

props.name: newspaper
props.note: The paper the man reads in the bathtub, unshivering in the cold.

props.name: cello
props.note: The instrument the cellist plays to the empty drained pool.

world.palette_rule: One warm yellow (#E7B93A) crosses every room — always the same hue, never the same object — and it is the only continuity the film gives you.
world.through_line: An unhurried, amused voice repeats 'luxury is—' over centered, symmetrical tableaux that each finish somewhere impossible and are abandoned on the cut, the definitions growing more private until the last one holds and hands the definition to you.

summary: An unhurried, amused voice keeps beginning the sentence "Luxury is…" and every time it finishes somewhere it shouldn't — spoken over a run of impossibly calm, symmetrical rooms: a man reading the paper in a bathtub on a snowing roof, a woman eating breakfast alone at a table set for twelve, a cellist playing to a drained pool. One warm yellow object threads through every room — a towel, a lemon, a lampshade, a robe — the only thing that carries over, and nobody points it out. The definitions grow more private until one is so specific it can only belong to a single man, standing in a lit walk-in closet choosing nothing. Then the room empties, the yellow stays, and the last line hands the definition to you.
premise: Luxury isn't a checklist of things — it's the private, faintly absurd freedom to want nothing, and it's yours to define.
ending: It lands on the empty walk-in closet — the man gone, one warm-yellow sleeve still on the rail — as the voice says "For you to define."

scenes.title: The voice starts
scenes.what_happens: From black, a symmetrical wide fades up: a clawfoot bathtub centered on a flat, snow-covered rooftop, a small figure reading a newspaper, steam holding its shape in the still cold air. The room reads before the man does. The voice begins the sentence and lets it hang, unfinished.
scenes.camera: Wide symmetrical tableau, slow push-in up from black, eye-level, deep focus.
scenes.why_it_lands: The unfinished sentence hands the viewer the game in one line — they lean in to finish it themselves.

shots.what_happens: From black, a drained infinity pool fades up head-on and empty, its long basin falling away symmetrically toward a hilltop villa. Clean and still.
shots.camera: EWS, dead-centered, eye-level, deep focus, a slow push up from black.

shots.what_happens: A long twelve-seat dining room snaps in for an instant — the table running straight down the center of frame, chairs mirrored on both walls.
shots.camera: WS, symmetrical, eye-level, locked — a hard-cut flash.

shots.what_happens: A lit walk-in closet flashes up — neutral garments ranked symmetrically down both sides, the aisle dead center.
shots.camera: WS, symmetrical, eye-level, locked — a hard-cut flash.

shots.what_happens: The snow-covered rooftop settles in: a clawfoot tub centered against falling snow, a small figure just readable inside it. The frame holds, handing the film forward.
shots.camera: WS, symmetrical, eye-level, deep focus, the push-in easing to a hold.

scenes.title: Warm where you shouldn't be
scenes.what_happens: We stay on the rooftop tub as the snow keeps falling and the man never shivers — the paper turns, the steam holds. The voice finally completes the first definition, and it lands somewhere absurd. On the cut, the whole impossible set is simply abandoned.
scenes.narration: Luxury is being warm somewhere you've no business being warm.
scenes.camera: Eye-level, deep focus; the push-in settles, then a hard cut walks away from the set.
scenes.why_it_lands: An impossible image kept perfectly calm proves the film's contract: it will show, never explain.

shots.what_happens: Extreme close on the top edge of the newspaper as a page turns, steam curling up past it and holding its shape in the cold.
shots.camera: ECU, eye-level, shallow focus on the paper's edge, no move.

shots.what_happens: The man, low in the water, reads on without a shiver as snow settles on his shoulders and hair.
shots.camera: MCU, eye-level, shallow focus, a breath of push-in.

shots.what_happens: The clawfoot tub whole in frame, the man low in the water, steam standing straight up in the still air.
shots.camera: MS from a high angle looking down into the tub, symmetrical, deep focus — the tub whole in frame, steam standing straight up toward the lens.

shots.what_happens: The entire impossible set at once — tub, man and steam marooned on a flat snowbound rooftop — held one beat, then gone on a hard cut.
shots.camera: WS, symmetrical, eye-level, deep focus; a hard cut away from the set.

morph.note: a white polar bear's head on his human body — dense wet-looking white fur, small dark eyes, black nose and lips, ears low and round; the skull heavy and correct, sitting naturally on a man's shoulders above the rim of the tub. He is still reading. He does not react. The water is what hides the change; nothing else in the frame moves for it.
morph.cover: he sinks below the surface — the water closes over the head and for a beat there is nothing but the moving surface and the steam above it — and then he rises back up in the same place, at the same height, and the head that breaks the surface is the polar bear's, water running off it. The newspaper stays exactly where it was

scenes.title: The yellow arrives
scenes.what_happens: Tight macro on a single lemon resting on black marble, warm yellow glowing against the dark stone. A rack of focus, then a match-cut to a yellow robe in another room — same hue, different object. The voice names none of it; the pattern is left for the eye to catch.
scenes.narration: Luxury is a detail you're fairly sure you weren't meant to notice.
scenes.camera: Tight macro, slow rack focus; match-cut on the yellow into the next room.
scenes.why_it_lands: The viewer clocks the thread themselves — a private reward that makes them an accomplice, not an audience.

shots.what_happens: Macro on a single lemon resting on black marble, its warm yellow glowing hard against the dark stone.
shots.camera: ECU macro, eye-level, shallow focus on the peel.

shots.what_happens: The focus racks slowly along the lemon, the yellow softening into a bloom of pure warm color.
shots.camera: CU, slow rack focus, no camera move.

shots.what_happens: Match-cut on the same yellow — now a robe draped over a chair in the long dining room, the hue carried straight across the cut.
shots.camera: MS, eye-level, deep focus, a match-cut on the color.

scenes.title: Alone, on purpose
scenes.what_happens: Pull wide on a twelve-seat dining table, warm yellow lampshades running its length, one woman eating breakfast at the near end. Eleven places are set and untouched. Nothing is wrong; the emptiness is plainly the point.
scenes.narration: Luxury is a table laid for twelve, and no intention of filling it.
scenes.camera: Centered wide, locked slow dolly-in, eye-level, deep focus.
scenes.why_it_lands: The empty seats read as chosen, not lonely — luxury as the power to leave eleven places empty.

shots.what_happens: Close on one untouched place setting — polished silver squared to the cloth, a warm yellow lampshade glowing just behind it.
shots.camera: CU, eye-level, shallow focus, holding still.

shots.what_happens: A single woman eats breakfast at the near end of the long table, small against the empty room.
shots.camera: MS, eye-level, deep focus, a locked slow dolly-in.

shots.what_happens: The full table revealed — yellow lampshades running its length, eleven places set and untouched, the woman alone at the far end.
shots.camera: EWS, centered, symmetrical, eye-level, deep focus, the dolly-in continuing.
shots.vo: and no intention of filling it.

morph.note: a giraffe's head on her human body — tan and cream reticulated hide, ossicones, long lashes over dark eyes, muzzle level and calm; the neck lengthens only as far as the frame needs and rises out of her collar as if it had always been hers. She goes on eating.
morph.cover: as the camera pulls wide, the nearest yellow lampshade swings through the foreground and passes fully across her head — one beat of nothing but the shade — and clears to the giraffe's head, already level and calm

scenes.title: The absurd escalation
scenes.what_happens: Low, wide angle across a drained infinity pool, hilltop villa behind. A cellist plays mid-basin, ankle-deep in the last film of water, a yellow cushion left on a lounger at the rim. She plays her whole heart out and there is no one to hear it.
scenes.narration: Luxury is playing your whole heart out to absolutely no one.
scenes.camera: Low wide angle, slow push-in, deep focus, figure small enough to read the whole basin.
scenes.why_it_lands: The absurdity peaks — a private concert for no one — and the definitions visibly slip past reason.

shots.what_happens: Close on the bow drawing across the cello's strings, the cellist's hands working with full feeling.
shots.camera: CU, eye-level, shallow focus on the strings, a faint push-in.
shots.vo: Luxury is playing your whole heart out

shots.what_happens: Low and wide across the drained infinity pool: she plays alone in the empty basin, ankle-deep in the last film of water, a yellow cushion left on a lounger at the rim, villa above.
shots.camera: EWS, low angle, deep focus, slow push-in, the figure small in the basin.

morph.note: a flamingo's head on the cellist's human body — pale coral plumage tight to the skull, the heavy black-tipped bill lowered toward the strings, one dark eye; the neck curves down to the instrument the way a player's does. The bow never stops.
morph.cover: her bow arm and the cello's neck sweep up across her face on a long stroke and hold there for a beat, hiding the head completely; as the arm comes down the flamingo's head is lowered to the strings, still playing

scenes.title: The closet — choosing nothing
scenes.what_happens: A man stands centered in a lit walk-in closet, rows of garments symmetrical on either side, one yellow sleeve breaking the neutral rail. His hands are at his sides; he chooses nothing, just stands there. The push-in stops opening out, and the shot holds past comfort.
scenes.narration: Luxury is standing in front of everything you own, and wanting none of it.
scenes.camera: Slow push-in, eye-level, shallow focus falling off past his shoulders; holds past comfort.
scenes.why_it_lands: The camera stops widening and traps us with one man — so specific it can only be his, and almost yours.

shots.what_happens: Close on a single yellow sleeve breaking a long neutral rail, chrome bar bright beside it, the man's idle hand just in frame below.
shots.camera: CU, eye-level, shallow focus on the sleeve, no move.
shots.vo: Luxury is standing in front of everything you own,

shots.what_happens: The man centered in the lit closet, symmetrical rows of clothes to either side, hands at his sides — he reaches for nothing and the frame holds past comfort.
shots.camera: WS, symmetrical, eye-level, shallow focus falling off past his shoulders, a slow push-in that opens out and holds.

morph.note: a peacock's head on his human body — iridescent blue-green throat feathers, the fine crest upright, a small pale eye; the head turned to the rail of clothes he is not choosing. The wardrobe behind him is plumage he has no use for.
morph.cover: a long hanging coat on the near rail swings into the foreground and passes right across him, blacking out the head for a beat; as it swings back the peacock's head is there, turned to the clothes he is not choosing

scenes.title: Handed back
scenes.what_happens: The same closet, everything identical — except the figure is gone. Nothing moves. The single yellow sleeve still hangs, dead center on the rail, soft bloom on the chrome. The voice hands the sentence over and the frame holds, then goes out.
scenes.camera: Static wide, no movement, deep focus, soft bloom on the rail chrome; hold, then out.
scenes.why_it_lands: The empty room plus the surviving yellow turns the definition over to the viewer — the seat is open.

shots.what_happens: The same closet, identical and still — but the man is gone. The one yellow sleeve still hangs dead center on the rail, soft bloom on the chrome. The frame holds, then goes out.
shots.camera: EWS from a high angle, symmetrical, static, deep focus — the whole closet from above the door line, the rail running away below. Hold, then out.
